tip.title: Do three one-minute bursts of hard effort
tip.why: In a study of about 25,000 adults who did no leisure exercise, those whose wearable data showed around three one-to-two-minute bursts of vigorous activity a day had roughly 38 to 40 percent lower risk of dying over the follow-up than those with none. It is observational, so it shows an association, but it suggests short bursts are worth trying on a busy day.
how: Pick something that gets you breathing hard: stairs, a fast uphill walk or a brisk carry.
Go hard for 60 seconds, three times spread across the day.
Add a bout whenever you are already moving, such as before a meeting or on the way to the car.
tip.ask: What does the research say about very short bursts of vigorous activity, and how strong is the evidence that they cause better health?

markets.headline: Stocks rose on Monday after Anthropic's IPO filing, with the Nasdaq up 0.8% and Tesla up 5.2% on a Barclays upgrade.
points: Anthropic's IPO filing revived enthusiasm for AI and chip stocks: the Nasdaq gained 0.8%, the S&P 500 0.7%, and the PHLX semiconductor index rose more than 3% after a weak October.
Meta said it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity for AI data centers and related infrastructure, which weighed on sentiment even as the broader tech group rallied.
Tesla jumped 5.2% to $391.62 after Barclays upgraded it to Overweight and raised its target to $450 from $370, citing possible SpaceX merger value and a recovery in autos.
WTI crude fell 1.8% to $101.48 and the 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.99%. A Fed decision and more big-tech earnings come later this week.

pick.name: Seagate Technology
pick.what: Seagate makes hard disk drives and storage systems, with large data-center customers that store the data behind cloud and AI services.
pick.why: It rose 2.2% on Oct 26 to $644.21 after falling roughly 30% over the past month, and the consensus of 26 analysts reads Strong Buy with an average target near $1,138. Barclays kept a Buy with a $1,250 target and Bank of America a Buy with $1,200 on Oct 21. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: The stock is still far below its 52-week high of $1,145, and a roughly 30% drop in a month shows how fast sentiment can turn. UBS rates it Hold, and demand depends on AI data-center spending holding up.

btc.summary: In his Oct 25 video, "Bitcoin: Bears Regaining Control," and in posts around it, Cowen said two straight weekly closes below the level he had been watching confirm that the September breakout was a fakeout, and that the rally has now been fully unwound. His next downside reference is the bull market support band, the zone formed by the 20-week average and 21-week exponential average. He ticked off two of nine steps on a bearish Q4 roadmap tied to the pattern of weakness late in US midterm years, and said the roadmap is void only if Bitcoin reclaims and holds that level. The next steps depend on the Fed decision and inflation data.

news.title: Tesla says Optimus production has started in Fremont
news.blurb: Tesla describes its California Optimus operation as in an early ramp phase, with hardware and manufacturing processes still evolving. Tech Times notes the robot has no buyers yet, and the news came alongside a 43% drop in quarterly profit.
news.ask: What does an early-ramp Optimus line in Fremont tell us about how fast humanoid manufacturing can scale, and what has to be true before there are paying customers?

news.title: GXO extends Agility's Digit humanoids to North Carolina and Tennessee
news.blurb: After Digit moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO's Georgia site, GXO will deploy the humanoids at two more US sites, with operations scheduled to begin in early 2027.
news.ask: Is a 100,000-tote milestone the kind of evidence a warehouse operator needs to scale humanoids, and what metrics would you want to see next?

news.title: Bedrock Robotics raises $600M at a $4.1B valuation for self-driving excavators
news.blurb: The two-year-old company says its autonomous excavators now run fully autonomously on live customer sites. CapitalG and Emergence Capital co-led the Series C.
news.ask: What does the speed of Bedrock's valuation jump say about investor appetite for physical AI outside humanoids, and what can humanoid teams learn from its job-site deployments?

news.title: Anthropic files for an IPO
news.blurb: The filing reports $16.29 billion in revenue for the six months ended June and warns of potentially catastrophic risks from AI. Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq as ANT, with a debut as soon as Nov 16 according to reports.
news.ask: How might a public Anthropic change competition with OpenAI and the funding landscape for AI and robotics startups?

news.title: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with GPT-6.1 Terra
news.blurb: The new model is aimed at speed and computer use at a lower price, with API pricing starting at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
news.ask: If computer use gets this much cheaper, which workflows become worth automating first, and how does it change what agents can do for robot software teams?

news.title: Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity for AI infrastructure
news.blurb: One report says Meta is launching $35 billion in common and preferred stock with a further $60 billion share sale planned later. Another says Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD have expressed interest in buying up to $5 billion of the shares.
news.ask: What does a mega-cap issuing equity, not debt, for AI data centers say about how the cost of the AI build-out is being financed?

news.title: Barclays upgrades Tesla to Overweight, raising its target to $450
news.blurb: Analyst Dan Levy cited possible value from a Tesla and SpaceX combination and a recovery in the core auto business. Tesla rose about 5% on Monday.
news.ask: How much of Tesla's move is merger speculation versus operating progress, and where do Optimus and robotaxi fit in that story?

news.title: SpaceX agrees to a roughly $40B equipment lease with Apollo to buy Nvidia GPUs
news.blurb: Bloomberg reports the financing will fund GPU purchases, according to a Tech Startups roundup. The roundup did not link the original Bloomberg report, so treat the details as secondhand.
news.ask: Why would SpaceX finance GPUs through a lease, and what does it suggest about its AI ambitions next to Tesla and xAI?

vocab.def: Lasting for a very short time.
vocab.ex: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.

cards.b: Greek ephemeros, 'lasting a day', from epi 'on' and hemera 'day'
fleeting, transient, short-lived
things that are expected to disappear quickly, like trends, moments, messages or blossoms

examples: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.
Some chat apps make messages ephemeral by deleting them after a day.

vocab.def: Using very few words; brief and to the point.
vocab.ex: Her laconic reply, 'Shipped,' told the team everything they needed to know.

cards.b: Greek Lakonikos, 'of Laconia', the region of Sparta, whose people were known for short, blunt speech
terse, succinct, concise
describing a person, a reply or a style of writing that says a lot in few words

examples: Her laconic reply, 'Shipped,' told the team everything they needed to know.
He was a laconic host, but nobody ever left his dinners hungry or confused.

vocab.def: Showing steady, careful and persistent effort.
vocab.ex: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.

cards.b: Latin sedulus, diligent or attentive
diligent, assiduous, industrious
praising careful, patient work, like testing, editing or research

examples: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.
Her sedulous note-taking meant nothing from the meeting was lost.

vocab.def: Friendly, lively and welcoming, especially of a gathering, a host or an atmosphere around food and drink.
vocab.ex: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.

cards.b: Latin convivium, a feast: con- (together) plus vivere (to live)
sociable, genial, festive
describing a party, a dinner, a host or the mood of a room

examples: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.
She is a convivial host who always makes sure everyone has a drink and someone to talk to.

vocab.def: Most noticeable or important; standing out from the rest.
vocab.ex: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.

cards.b: Latin salire, to leap: a salient fact leaps out at you
prominent, key, striking
naming the main point in a report, a meeting or a demo

examples: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.
Skip the background and lead with the three salient numbers.

vocab.def: Mental calm and evenness of temper, especially under stress.
vocab.ex: She handled the delayed flight with equanimity, reading a book while everyone else queued at the desk.

cards.b: Latin aequus, even, plus animus, mind: an even mind
composure, poise, calm
how you take delays, bad news or a long travel day

examples: She handled the delayed flight with equanimity, reading a book while everyone else queued at the desk.
The best on-call engineers meet a 3 a.m. page with equanimity, not panic.

vocab.def: Calmly optimistic, especially when things look uncertain.
vocab.ex: The team stayed sanguine about the demo, even after the gripper missed twice in rehearsal.

cards.b: Latin sanguis, blood: a 'sanguine' temperament was once blamed on blood
upbeat, unworried, confident
sanguinary means bloodthirsty

examples: The team stayed sanguine about the demo, even after the gripper missed twice in rehearsal.
She's more sanguine about the market than I am; she thinks last week's sell-off was mostly nerves.

spanish.note: 'Bronca' means trouble or a problem in casual Mexican Spanish. Say it to wave off an apology or reassure someone; it is friendly and informal.

dialog.en: Sorry, I got here late.
No problem! We just started.
Thanks, I already have the coffee.
Perfect, sit down.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend apologizes for being late or asks if a small favor is okay.

spanish.note: 'Chido' is very common casual Mexican slang for cool or great. It is friendly and informal, fine with friends and peers.

dialog.en: Did you see my new car?
Yes! Your car is so cool!
Thanks, I bought it yesterday.
How nice! Congratulations.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend shows you something you like, like a car, a phone or a new place.

options: Where did you park your car?

spanish.phrase: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
spanish.pron: ah-oh-REE-tah VEN-goh, voy por OO-nohs TAH-kohs
spanish.meaning: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
spanish.note: 'Ahorita' is flexible in Mexico: it can mean right now or a while from now, depending on tone. 'Ahorita vengo' is the usual way to say you are stepping out and coming back soon.

cards.en: I'll be back in a bit

parts.en: in a little while / right now

dialog.en: Where are you going?

dialog.es: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos.
dialog.en: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
Can you bring me two al pastor?
Sure, I'll bring them in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it when you step out of a room or a shop for a few minutes and plan to come back.

options: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
I already ate all the tacos.

spanish.note: The standard cheer at a Mexican wedding toast, shouted by the whole room. 'Novios' means the bride and groom, or a couple who are engaged or newly married. It's for weddings and anniversaries.

dialog.en: It's time for the toast!
Cheers! Long live the newlyweds!
And may they dance all night!
Exactly! Now, to the dance floor.

spanish.use: Say it when someone raises a glass at a wedding, or after a friend announces an engagement.

options: The bus leaves in five minutes.

spanish.phrase: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
spanish.pron: nee MOH-doh, yah seh-RAH PAH-rah lah PROHK-see-mah
spanish.meaning: Oh well, there's always next time.
spanish.note: 'Ni modo' is the everyday Mexican shrug for something that can't be changed. Add 'ya será para la próxima' after a missed plan to move on lightly; it's not for serious losses.

dialog.es: Se canceló el partido por la lluvia.
dialog.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.

dialog.es: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima.
dialog.en: Oh well, there's always next time.
Want to go get tacos then?
Now you're talking! My treat.

spanish.use: Say it when a plan falls through and you'd rather move on than complain, like a missed flight or a canceled game.

options: Oh well, there's always next time.

spanish.note: 'No manches' is the everyday Mexican way to say 'no way' or 'you're kidding', and 'padre' means great. Friendly with friends; keep it out of formal settings.

dialog.es: Mira, conseguí boletos para el concierto.
dialog.en: Look, I got tickets for the concert.
No way, that's really cool!
And we have spots up front.
No way! When is it?

spanish.use: Say it next time a friend shares good news, instead of 'wow'.

spanish.note: The everyday Mexican hello between friends. 'Onda' literally means wave, as in vibe. A relaxed reply is 'Nada, aquí nomás.'

dialog.en: What's up! How have you been?
Good, nothing new. And you?

spanish.use: Open your next text to a friend with it instead of 'hey'.

Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
